Description: Hooks-based functional components are the modern standard in React
Do: Write all components as functions using hooks
Don't: Write class-based components for new code

Description: Each component should do one thing and do it well
Do: Split large components into focused smaller ones
Don't: Build monolithic components handling many concerns

Guideline: Lift state to closest common ancestor
Description: Share state between siblings by lifting it up one level
Do: Lift state to the parent that needs it
Don't: Duplicate state in sibling components
Code Bad: Each sibling owns its own copy of shared state

Description: Pass components as children or slots instead of deeply nesting props
Do: Use children or render props for flexible composition
Don't: Prop drill more than 2-3 levels deep

Description: Type all props with TypeScript interfaces for safety and DX
Do: Define an interface or type for every component's props
Don't: Use untyped props or PropTypes in new code
Code Good: interface Props { label: string; onClick: () => void }

Guideline: Use useState for local UI state
Description: Simple local state belongs in useState not in global stores
Do: useState for form inputs toggles and local UI
Don't: Put all state into a global store

Description: When state transitions have multiple cases useReducer is clearer
Do: useReducer when next state depends on current state logic
Don't: Multiple related useState calls with coordinated updates

Description: Context re-renders all consumers on every change; use it for slow-changing values
Do: Context for theme locale auth user data
Don't: Context for high-frequency state like form fields or animations

Guideline: Use Zustand for global client state
Description: Zustand is minimal and avoids Context re-render pitfalls
Do: Zustand or Jotai for shared client state
Don't: Redux for new projects without complex middleware needs
Code Bad: new store with redux boilerplate for simple state

Guideline: Derive values instead of syncing state
Description: Computed values should derive from existing state not be stored separately
Do: Compute derived values inline or with useMemo
Don't: Store derived state and keep it in sync with useEffect
Code Bad: const [fullName] = useState(first + last) + useEffect to sync

Description: Wrap components in React.memo to skip re-renders when props are unchanged
Do: memo() on components that receive stable props
Don't: memo() on every component by default

Description: Stable function references prevent child re-renders
Do: useCallback for handlers passed as props to memoized children
Don't: useCallback for every function regardless of usage
Code Bad: const handle = useCallback(() => {}, []) on every handler

Description: Avoid recomputing heavy work on every render
Do: useMemo for CPU-intensive derivations
Don't: useMemo for cheap calculations like adding two numbers

Description: Load large components only when needed to reduce initial bundle size
Do: React.lazy + Suspense for routes and heavy modals
Don't: Import all components eagerly at the top level
Code Bad: import Chart from './Chart' in the root bundle

Description: Render only visible items to avoid DOM bloat
Do: TanStack Virtual or react-window for lists over 100 items
Don't: Render thousands of DOM nodes with Array.map

Guideline: Prefer CSS Modules for scoped styles
Description: CSS Modules scope class names at build time with zero runtime cost
Do: CSS Modules for component-level styles
Don't: Global CSS for component-specific styles

Description: Tailwind avoids context-switching and keeps styles co-located in JSX
Do: Tailwind for new projects; use design tokens via config
Don't: Mix Tailwind with arbitrary inline styles freely

Guideline: Avoid dynamic inline styles for layout
Description: Inline styles bypass CSS optimizations and cause re-renders
Do: Keep layout in CSS/Tailwind; use inline only for truly dynamic values
Don't: Use inline style objects for static layout

Description: Dedicated data-fetching libraries handle caching deduplication and revalidation
Do: React Query or SWR for all server state
Don't: Manual fetch in useEffect with local loading/error state
Code Good: const { data } = useQuery({ queryKey: ['user'] queryFn: fetchUser })

Guideline: Never fetch in useEffect for initial data
Description: useEffect fetching is prone to race conditions and lacks caching
Do: Use a data-fetching library for initial page data
Don't: useEffect(() => { fetch(...) } []) as the primary data strategy

Guideline: Always handle loading and error states
Description: Users need feedback; unhandled rejections cause white screens
Do: Render loading skeletons and error messages
Don't: Assume fetch always succeeds

Guideline: Use error boundaries for async errors
Description: Error boundaries catch rendering errors from async data in Suspense
Do: Wrap suspense trees with an ErrorBoundary component
Don't: Let unhandled errors crash the whole page
Code Bad: No error boundary around data-dependent subtrees

Description: Semantic elements communicate role to assistive technologies natively
Do: button for actions; a for navigation; label for inputs
Don't: div and span for interactive elements

Description: Screen readers announce labels; unlabeled controls are unusable
Do: htmlFor on label tied to input id; aria-label on icon buttons
Don't: Rely on placeholder text as the only visible label

Description: When content changes or modals open users must be guided to new content
Do: Move focus to modal on open; return focus on close
Don't: Let focus stay on the triggering element behind an overlay

Guideline: Announce dynamic content with ARIA live regions
Description: Changes that appear without user action need aria-live to be announced
Do: aria-live="polite" for status messages and toast notifications
Don't: Update content silently with no live region

Description: Controlled inputs keep React as the single source of truth for form values
Do: value + onChange for all inputs
Don't: defaultValue without controlled state for important forms

Guideline: Use React Hook Form for complex forms
Description: RHF minimizes re-renders and integrates validation libraries
Do: React Hook Form for forms with 3+ fields or validation
Don't: Manually manage all field state and validation
Code Bad: useState for every field + custom validation

Description: Schema validation gives type-safe runtime checks and integrates with RHF
Do: Zod + zodResolver for form validation
Don't: Hand-rolled if/else validation per field

Description: Display errors next to the relevant field immediately after interaction
Do: Show errors below each field on blur or submit
Don't: Show one alert-box with all errors at the top

Description: RTL encourages testing from the user's perspective via accessible queries
Do: getByRole getByLabelText getByText for queries
Don't: getByTestId or shallow rendering for most tests

Description: user-event simulates real browser interactions including focus and keyboard
Do: userEvent.type userEvent.click for all interactions
Don't: fireEvent directly for interactions that involve real user behavior

Description: Tests should survive refactors; test what users see and do
Do: Assert on rendered output and accessible state
Don't: Assert on internal state or component method calls
